approach:
Root cause: the producer's per-run wall-clock limit (`budget.producer_timeout_s`, passed to `agent_spec` at crates/athena-core/src/run/producer.rs:344, stored as `spec.timeout` at crates/athena-core/src/reading.rs:457, enforced at crates/athena-agent/src/claude.rs:592) was never told to the producer. Its brief and prompt state no limit, so the stage could not pace itself against it. The pacing rules it already has (targeted tests; the suite at most once, crates/athena-context/prompts/producer.md:9; full-suite criteria left to Athena's checks, briefs.rs:856-858) were never tied to a limit.

The change adds one `## Time budget` section to the producer brief. A new `ProducerInputs.deadline_s: u64` feeds it. One accessor, `producer_deadline_s(jc)` in producer.rs, supplies the number both to the invocation (producer.rs:344) and to the brief builder (run/mod.rs:1178). The two cannot drift: the producer loop and dispatch share one `JobConfig` (`RunContext { jc: &jc }`, mod.rs:1301). The section renders unconditionally, so a fresh job, a seeded retry, an unseeded retry, a stale-conflict retry and a timeout resume all carry it. A send-back is the brief plus `## Sent back` (send_back.rs:136), so it carries it too.

Answers to the round-1 findings:
1. The criterion-3 test no longer asserts byte equality. The prompt differs from the stored brief by the evidence placeholder (mod.rs:1157, 1340) and an optional governing-decisions tail (mod.rs:1362). The test compares the extracted `## Time budget` section of both texts, requires "4321 seconds" in each, and checks `prompt.starts_with(stored.replace(placeholder, real_path))`. It keeps the assertions on `spec.timeout` and the record's `caps.timeout_s`.
2. The dependents now list the readers of the stored brief outside athena-core: athena-gate jobs.rs:287 and :489-511 and landing_tests.rs, athena-cli job_plan.rs:259-277 and lifecycle.rs:292, and athena-data records.rs:1451. Each has a reason and a test command.
3. The section leads with the limit and points to the existing rules. It gives no new reason to run the full suite. It keeps only the cap "at most once" (criterion 1 asks for it) and says Athena runs the suite again on the result (see "Checks before the verifier"), so a second full run only spends the limit. The root cause is worded as "the stage was never told its own per-run limit, so its existing pacing rules had nothing to hang on".
4. `date` is not in the producer's allowed commands (athena.toml:84 lists cargo, git, ls, rm, mv, chmod), so the brief cannot tell the producer to run it. The text says: if the Bash list below includes `date`, note the time at the start and read it between steps; otherwise pace by the order of work. The CHANGELOG records that the live limit is 86400 s (athena.toml:51) and that the information matters most if the limit is lowered again.

Prompt files, athena.toml, defaults.toml and the resume, stall and deadline code are untouched. No check, hold or refusal is added: the expected share of newly refused readings is 0%. No reading rule, parser or stem list changes, so no refusal_corpus case is added or mapped.

decisions.choice: Carry the deadline as one new `ProducerInputs.deadline_s: u64`, filled in core from a single accessor `producer_deadline_s(jc: &JobConfig) -> u64` in producer.rs that the invocation also uses (producer.rs:344). Reuse of the config key `budget.producer_timeout_s`: documented meaning and fit, quoted below.
decisions.reason:
The context crate depends only on data (system facts, Crate reach), so it cannot read the config and the number must arrive as an input. One accessor for the enforced and the stated value means they cannot drift (criterion 3).

Documented meaning of the key. `Budget.producer_timeout_s` is a bare `pub producer_timeout_s: u64` with no doc comment (crates/athena-data/src/config.rs:405). Its meaning is fixed by four places in the code and config. athena.toml:49 says 'Stage time limits are 24 hours: they do not stop work', with the key at athena.toml:51. `check_reading_size` (reading.rs:361-368) calls it the 'producer ... deadline' beyond which 'no single run can finish' a reading. `agent_spec` turns it into `Duration::from_secs(timeout_s)` (reading.rs:457). The driver enforces it as `deadline = clock + spec.timeout` and records 'deadline of {secs}s reached' (claude.rs:592, procs.rs:20-22). That is exactly the per-run limit the brief must state.

Live value for each role it could affect: producer_timeout_s = 86400 (athena.toml:51). The reader, verifier, planner and critic keys (athena.toml:50, 52, 224-225) are not read by this change. Because the live value is 86400, the brief states 86400 seconds today. That is true, and it stays true if the value is lowered.

rejected.why: The live athena.toml sets 86400 (athena.toml:51; CHANGELOG.md:12 raised it from the earlier limit). A constant is false today and would drift again, and the request asks for the configured value.

rejected.option: Read `budget.producer_timeout_s` separately in producer.rs and in mod.rs
rejected.why: Two reads of one key can drift. The shared accessor makes the criterion-3 test about one value.

decisions.choice: Put the text in the generated brief: a new `time_budget_section(deadline_s)` beside `no_change_section` (briefs.rs:757), called in `producer_brief_with_evidence` (briefs.rs:681) after `pin_section` and before `failure_classes_section`, unconditionally.
decisions.reason: Briefs sit outside the prompt-set token budgets (docs/system-facts.md; the producer set is 1043 of 1200), so no budget line or `system_facts_budgets_match_computed` moves. The brief is stored verbatim as brief-producer.md (mod.rs:1274), so a test can read it. Placing it before the banned-words and checks sections keeps the order checks the existing tests rely on (briefs.rs:2283-2284, 2303-2305, 2324-2328).

rejected.why: Out of scope. It moves the producer token budget and a pinned test.

decisions.choice: Word the section to lead with the per-run limit and tie the existing pacing rules to it, not to restate them as new rules. Fixed text: 'Each producer run, the first and any send-back, is stopped after {deadline_s} seconds of wall-clock time. A stopped run sends no report, so what is on disk when it stops must already be a usable change.' Then: 'Do the smallest change that meets every acceptance criterion first, one file at a time, ... report as soon as the criteria are met. Leave no half-edited file and no broken build between steps. Use targeted tests ... The full suite runs at most once, and Athena runs it again on your result (see "Checks before the verifier" below), so a second full run only spends this limit.'
decisions.reason: Answers finding 3. producer.md:9 already says to run targeted tests and the suite at most once, and briefs.rs:856-858 says a full-suite criterion is left to Athena's checks. The section keeps only the cap (acceptance criterion 1 asks for 'at most once') and gives the reason in terms of the limit, so it never tells the producer to run the full suite. It avoids the strings the existing producer-brief tests forbid: 'cost', '0.8', '0.97', 'p10' (briefs.rs:1557), 'reached its deadline' (1907), '## Retry' (1910, 1946), 'rejected candidate' (1851, 1948), 'starts from the base' (1939), 'sha:' (1966), and the boundary-scan words. It does not contain 'cargo test -p xtask --test policy' or 'cargo test -p athena-cli --test mirrors', whose first occurrence the tests at 2303 and 2324 require to sit after the banned-words section.

rejected.option: Tell the producer to run the full test suite once after the change is complete
rejected.why: Gives a new reason to run the full suite and pulls against briefs.rs:856-858 (finding 3).

decisions.choice: Give an elapsed-time reference conditionally on the brief's own command list: 'You have no clock of your own. If the commands Bash may run (below) include `date`, note the time when you start and read it between steps; without it, count steps against the order above.' Record in the CHANGELOG that the number matters most if the limit is lowered again (live value 86400 s).
decisions.reason: Answers finding 4. The producer's allowed commands are cargo, git, ls, rm, mv and chmod (athena.toml:84), so `date` is denied by the producer grant today. An unconditional instruction to run `date` would be wrong. Adding `date` to producer_commands means editing athena.toml, a governance file that is not a deliverable and is out of scope. The conditional sentence is true for any capability whose list holds `date`, and the 'Commands Bash may run' list in the same brief shows which it is.

rejected.option: Tell the producer to run `date` unconditionally
rejected.why: Denied by the producer's command grant (athena.toml:84), so the instruction would fail.
athena.toml is a governance file that is not a deliverable; out of scope.

decisions.choice: State the limit per run, not per job, and do not state the stall window.
decisions.reason: `spec` is rebuilt on every pass of the producer loop with the same timeout (producer.rs:329-346), so a send-back gets a fresh limit. The stall window is `(timeout / 3).max(floor)` (procs.rs:27-31) with a driver-set floor that tests lower (claude.rs:598, 1341). Printing it needs a second field that can drift, and pacing does not need it. The stall stop (claude.rs:596-619) and resume of a timed-out job (`timeout_seed`, `keep_unfinished_work`, mod.rs:883, 945) stay as backstops.

rejected.why: Adds a second field and a drift risk for no pacing gain.

decisions.choice: No refusal, hold, watchdog or retry rule. Expected share of past accepted readings newly refused: 0%.
decisions.reason: Giving the stage the number does not need a rule, and the request asks to prefer that. `check_reading_size` (reading.rs:370) already refuses a reading whose forecast median exceeds the deadline and is unchanged. No parser, stem list or reading check changes, so there is no input form to map to a refusal_corpus case and no `refusal_corpus` demonstration.

rejected.option: Refuse an identical-scope retry after a deadline, or add a progress watchdog or checkpoints
rejected.why: A refusal rule is allowed only when information cannot prevent the failure. Both are listed out of scope. The watchdog and resume already exist (claude.rs:596-619; mod.rs:883, 945).

risks.risk: The live athena.toml sets producer_timeout_s = 86400 (athena.toml:51; 'they do not stop work'), while the failures in the class happened at 1800 s. Today's brief says 86400 seconds, and a number that large gives the producer little to pace against, so behaviour may change less than the request expects.
risks.mitigation: The brief states whatever is configured, so it is true today and stays true if the value is lowered. The pacing text (order of work, tree always reportable, targeted tests) does not depend on the size of the number. The CHANGELOG says the 1800 s was the earlier value and the information matters most if the limit is lowered again.

risks.risk: The producer has no clock: `date` is not in its allowed commands (athena.toml:84), so it cannot measure elapsed time.
risks.mitigation: The text says so and offers the `date` reading only when the Bash list in the same brief includes it; otherwise it paces by the order of work. No governance file is edited. A real clock or progress signal is a follow-up (out of scope: watchdog, checkpoints).

risks.risk: A producer may ignore the pacing text, and nothing here measures whether it follows it.
risks.mitigation: The CHANGELOG says the effect is not measured. The stall stop (claude.rs:596-619) and resume of a timed-out job (mod.rs:883, 945) stay as backstops.

risks.mitigation: The fixed text in step 2 avoids all of them, and criterion 6 runs every one of those tests on the final tree. The producer fixes any hit before reporting.

demonstrations.method: New unit test `time_budget_states_each_jobs_own_deadline` in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs. It builds `producer_inputs(None)` and sets `deadline_s` to 300, then to 5400. It asserts the first brief contains 'is stopped after 300 seconds of wall-clock time' and not '5400 seconds', and the second the reverse. It asserts both contain 'smallest change that meets every acceptance criterion', 'at most once', 'no half-edited file' and '`date`'. It then builds five brief shapes at 300 seconds: fresh; seeded retry (`retry_from = Some(seed())`); resume (`RetrySeed { progress_note: Some(..), candidate: Some(..), ..seed() }`); stale conflict (`conflicts` non-empty); unseeded retry (`retry_findings = Some(RetryFindings { .. })`). For each it asserts `brief.matches("## Time budget").count() == 1` and the '300 seconds' text.
demonstrations.observes: Each brief carries its own number and the section appears exactly once in all five shapes. The two deadlines are not substrings of each other.
demonstrations.fails_without: On the base the test does not compile (`ProducerInputs.deadline_s` does not exist). With the field but a constant in the text, the brief for 5400 lacks '5400 seconds'. With the section only on the fresh path, the retry, resume or conflict shape lacks '## Time budget' and the count assertion fails.

demonstrations.method: New test `the_producer_deadline_in_the_stored_brief_is_the_one_the_invocation_runs_under` in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs. Steps: `repo()` (tests.rs:288); read its athena.toml, `replacen("producer_timeout_s = 86400", "producer_timeout_s = 4321", 1)` and assert the text changed (the line is athena.toml:51); commit with `commit_file` (tests.rs:358). Wrap `base_script()` in a `Script` closure that, for `Role::Producer`, records `spec.timeout.as_secs()` and `spec.user_prompt` and then calls the base script (the pattern at tests.rs:858-903). Run `athena_with(&repo, &state, PASSES, crate::test_support::plenty_of_space, script)`, then `ask("describe the demo", &Quiet)` and `go(..., AcceptedBy::User, &Quiet)`, and assert the job landed. Load `Records::load(&athena.git, &athena.head().unwrap())` and take `jobs[id]`. Assert: recorded `spec.timeout` is 4321; the producer entry in `job.invocations` has `caps.timeout_s == 4321` (written from `spec.timeout` at crates/athena-core/src/invocation.rs:212); the job record's `caps.producer_timeout_s == 4321`; the `## Time budget` section (from that heading to the next '\n## ') of `job.briefs["brief-producer"]` equals the same section of the recorded prompt and contains '4321 seconds'; the stored brief does not contain '86400'; and `prompt.starts_with(&stored.replace(&format!("<state>/jobs/{id}/evidence"), &state.path().join("repo/jobs").join(id).join("evidence").display().to_string()))`. The reader forecast has p50 = 30 s (tests.rs:245), under the 4321 limit that `check_reading_size` (reading.rs:370) applies, so the reading is accepted.
demonstrations.observes: The deadline the invocation ran under, the number recorded in the invocation and job records, and the number in the stored brief are all 4321. 4321 is neither the repository value (86400) nor a constant in the code, so a copy or a constant would show. The prompt is the stored brief with only the placeholder replaced.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the change the stored brief has no 'Time budget' section, so the '4321 seconds' assertion fails. If the brief took its number from another source (a constant, or the default 86400), the equality with `spec.timeout` and the '4321' assertion fail.

demonstrations.method: Read the CHANGELOG entry (new bullet at the top of the Added list under [Unreleased]; the Added heading is at CHANGELOG.md:20) and the doc comment on `time_budget_section`. Both must name the root cause: the producer stage was never told its own per-run limit, so it could not pace against it and its existing pacing rules had nothing to hang on. The entry must list jobs 20261010-154006-vc5k, 20261016-052605-qw38 and 20261018-070117-qmxv as addressed by this. It must say they recorded no candidate, so nothing is kept from them, and their original requests (verifier snapshot note, auditor and warden roles, baseline checks) are not redone. It must note that the 1800 s of the failure class is the earlier value, that the live limit is 86400 s (athena.toml:51, CHANGELOG.md:12), that the number matters most if the limit is lowered again, and that the producer has no `date` command under the default grant. It must name the tests and say no refusal rule is added (0% newly refused) and that whether producers follow the pacing text is not measured.
demonstrations.observes: Both texts name the root cause. The entry covers the three jobs, the 86400 value, the date limitation, the tests and the 0% figure.
